review_notes: I read the whole file. It declares no simp lemmas, so the review looked for missing simp lemmas. I checked the definitions behind the two clusters I flag: the helper defs `toSum` and `sumEnds`, and the Mathlib-style lemma `ModularCurve.baseAut_arithmeticGalois` in Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_ArithmeticGalois.lean. That lemma is already @[simp] and says `baseAut (arithmeticGalois F₀ σ) = σ.toRingEquiv`. I did not inspect every candidate simp lemma for the Sigma/Sum coercions, and I could not run Lean. I did not find any loops or competing rules. The suggested lemmas are untested, and the second finding is a weaker point than the first.

findings.excerpt:
def sumEnds : (CuspidalType.ProjLine q × ↥W) ⊕ (CuspidalType.ProjLine q × ↥W) → SumSigma 𝒞 :=
  Sum.elim (fun p => ⟨Sum.inl p.1, 𝒞.sumNode (Sum.inl p.1) p⟩) (fun p => ⟨Sum.inr p.2, 𝒞.sumNode (Sum.inr p.2) p⟩)
findings.problem: `toSum` and `sumEnds` are plain defs with no equation lemmas of their own, and no simp lemmas for them. Every later proof unfolds them by hand. `toSum_src` and `toSum_tgt` restate the whole unfolded Sigma term in a `show`. `exists_sumEnds_eq` and `sumEnds_unique` use six `change (⟨Sum.inl ℓ, 𝒞.xs ℓ s⟩ : SumSigma 𝒞) = ⟨j, x⟩ at hE`-style steps, again with the same terms written out. The canonical forms are not stated anywhere, so none of these proofs can use `simp`. `toSum_src` and `toSum_tgt` are also not simp lemmas, so a later `simp` cannot turn `toSum _ ⟨teleSrc e, teleXs e⟩` into `sumEnds _ (inl _)`.
findings.proposed_change: Add the defining equations as simp lemmas, for example `@[simp] theorem toSum_mk (i x) : toSum 𝒞 ⟨i, x⟩ = ⟨𝒞.eIdx.symm i, x⟩ := rfl`. Add `@[simp] theorem sumEnds_inl (p) : sumEnds 𝒞 (Sum.inl p) = ⟨Sum.inl p.1, 𝒞.sumNode (Sum.inl p.1) p⟩ := rfl`, and the matching `sumEnds_inr`. Then the `show` and `change` steps shrink to `simp` or `rw [sumEnds_inl]`. After that, mark `toSum_src` and `toSum_tgt` @[simp], with the left side as the tele-form and the right side as the sum-form, to match how `tele_nodes` and `toSum_elim` already use them.
findings.benefit: Readers no longer see the same large Sigma term repeated in six places. The proofs stop depending on definitional unfolding. Later users of the telescope frame get a stable normal form for `sumEnds` and `toSum`.

evidence.excerpt: change (⟨Sum.inl ℓ, 𝒞.xs ℓ s⟩ : SumSigma 𝒞) = ⟨j, x⟩ at hE

findings.excerpt:
SemilinearAut.baseAut (ModularCurve.arithmeticGalois (L := AlgebraicClosure ℚ) (F0 q M') τ) a = τ a := by
  rw [ModularCurve.baseAut_arithmeticGalois]
  rfl
findings.problem: The library already has the simp lemma `baseAut_arithmeticGalois`, which gives `σ.toRingEquiv`. This local lemma only adds the pointwise form, and it is not tagged @[simp]. So a `simp` call cannot reach `baseAut (arithmeticGalois _ τ) a = τ a` without a manual rewrite plus `rfl`. The statement is also pinned to the local abbrev `F0`, although the proof uses nothing about `F0`.
findings.proposed_change: Generalise the statement over any `F₀ : IntermediateField ℚ (LaurentSeries ℚ)`. Mark it @[simp], or drop it and let `simp` finish with the existing simp lemma `baseAut_arithmeticGalois` plus the `AlgEquiv.toRingEquiv` coercion simp lemmas. The pointwise lemma belongs next to `baseAut_arithmeticGalois` in Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_ArithmeticGalois.lean. In `solution`, `hbase` could then be `fun a => by simp [hsτ]`, or a single `rw [hsτ]; exact baseAut_arithmeticGalois_apply ..`.
findings.benefit: The simp set gets the pointwise form for any base field. The `rw ...; rfl` step in the proof goes away. Other files that use `arithmeticGalois` can reuse the lemma instead of rediscovering it.
